description: `(:x) = 2` (issue #442/F3): assigning to a fully-parenthesized colon target raises the runtime's own `ol-not-a-place`, reached through `execute()`'s own check before Phase 2 (mirroring `not-a-place-runtime-postfix-expression.expected.json`'s postfix case). The parser re-wraps the grouping-stripped `(:x)` into a zero-segment `PostfixExpression`, so `executeAssign`'s non-`Place` guard fires and `not-a-place-text.ts`'s runtime-side `PostfixExpressionNode` renderer produces the same full target text `(:x)` the checker renders. `:x` is never read: the non-place target is rejected before the assignment's value or base is evaluated, and since issue #815 before the program runs at all. Issue #815: `execute()` now runs Layer 1 and Layer 2 before Phase 2 and refuses a program carrying an `error`-severity finding (`spec/execution-model.md:659-664`), so no event is emitted and the diagnostic delivered here is the CHECK's. The runtime's own copy of the rule still exists and still runs — under the `runUnchecked` opt-out — and is collapsed into the check's by the de-duplication rule (`spec/execution-model.md:741-748`), which is why the runtime's copy does not appear beside the check's. The other findings recorded here are independent faults in the same program, each reported once.
